body:
Hash joins can repeat build-side values, causing functions such as `list_sort` to repeat work. This broadens reusable dictionary output for scalar payloads and enables it for small builds with `LIST` or `MAP` payloads when an output chunk covers every build entry.

The original proposal changed optimizer expression placement. We chose dictionary emission because existing dictionary function execution can reuse results for repeated build values without adding LIST-width costing or aggregate-expression placement rules. The same mechanism applies across eligible functions and payloads.

Fixes #28179.

<details>
<summary>Previous proposal (superseded)</summary>

The description below documents the original optimizer implementation and its validation.

**Original title:** Avoid repeated list sorting after fan-out joins

Fixes #28179.

Projection pull-up and aggregate projection fusion can leave `list_sort` above a fan-out join. Add overflow-checked LIST width costing for known maximum lengths and fixed-size elements, and expose safe LIST-dependent scalar aggregate arguments to existing cost-based placement. Keep the existing 0.75 threshold and fallback for unsupported statistics; deduplicate shared arguments.

Evidence against `6145a8699b` (macOS arm64, 4 threads, 2 GB, default optimizers): **2,047.5 → 82.5 ms median (24.8×)** across 10 measured runs per binary, reversing execution order; identical checksum. Profiled sort input falls from **200,000 → 2,000 rows**. Cheap scalar and bounded-string controls retain baseline medians (24/14 ms).

Fresh RelWithDebInfo build; **460 assertions passed across 8 targeted test files**; clang-format and diff checks passed. Regression coverage includes placement, shared arguments without CSE, NULL/empty lists, grouping/filter bindings, and unsupported nested/string lists. Full CI and broad benchmark suites remain pending. Fork validation: [kevintruong/duckdb#3](https://github.com/kevintruong/duckdb/pull/3), [CI running](https://github.com/kevintruong/duckdb/actions/runs/43079553692).

AI-assisted implementation and validation.


</details>

linked_issues.body:
### What happens?

On 1.5.6, the query below sorts 2,000 lists before joining. On `ed0443f18a`, sorting moves above the join and executes on 200,000 rows instead.

Same machine, four threads, second execution excluding data preparation:

| Version / setting | Time |
|---|---:|
| 1.5.6 (`069cc9f9b5`) | 0.035 s |
| `ed0443f18a`, default settings | 0.981 s |
| `ed0443f18a`, `projection_pullup` disabled | 0.029 s |

The development build is approximately **28× slower**. All executions return:

```text
28496903230666301809900
```

These are CLI wall-clock measurements. The development results refer to the tested local Release build; upstream HEAD was not rebuilt.

### To Reproduce

```sql
SET threads = 4;
SET memory_limit = '2GB';

CREATE TABLE lists AS
SELECT
    i AS id,
    list_transform(
        range(128),
        lambda x: hash(i * 128 + x)::UBIGINT
    ) AS vals
FROM range(2000) t(i);

CREATE TABLE fanout AS
SELECT i % 2000 AS id
FROM range(200000) t(i);

-- Run twice, then inspect with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
SELECT sum(sorted_values[1]::HUGEINT) AS checksum
FROM (
    SELECT id, list_sort(vals) AS sorted_values
    FROM lists
) l
JOIN fanout f ON l.id = f.id;
```

On the development build, repeat the query after:

```sql
SET disabled_optimizers = 'projection_pullup';
```

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` shows that disabling this optimizer moves `list_sort` back below the join, reducing its input from 200,000 rows to 2,000 rows without changing the result.

### OS:

macOS 27.0.1, arm64.

### DuckDB Version:

Homebrew 1.5.6 (`069cc9f9b5`) and local Release build `ed0443f18a` (v2.1.0-dev90926).

### DuckDB Client:

CLI. The development CLI was launched with `-no-agent`.

### Hardware:

Apple M1 Max, 32 GiB RAM. Query settings: 4 threads, memory_limit='2GB'.

### Full Name:

wangqiang

### Affiliation:
